entities.summary: The Taoiseach was a public office in Ireland, a significant occurrence during the Classical era. Established in 1205, it was a key figure associated with the governance of the Irish monarchy. The position was created to unify Ireland under a single ruler and was characterized by a complex system of alliances and rivalries with neighboring kingdoms. The Taoiseach played a crucial role in the medieval Irish wars, with notable figures such as Brian Boru and Cormac MacCarthy wielding the office. This institution had a lasting impact on Irish politics, with the modern-day Taoiseach being a direct descendant of the medieval position. The Taoiseach was also closely tied to the Church of Ireland, with the Archbishop of Dublin holding significant influence over the office. The office's legacy can still be seen in the current Irish government, with the Taoiseach serving as the head of government and chief advisor to the President of Ireland.
